Subject: POC plan + success criteria — Acme Health (next steps & RACI)

Hi Rachel / Tom —

Thanks again for the time today — great discussion. Per our call, I wanted to capture the agreed next steps for the Proof of Concept (POC) so we have clarity on success criteria, timeline, and ownership. Please review and flag anything missing.

Summary of what we discussed:
- POC objective: Validate Redwood inference for clinical triage feature (lower-latency routing + high precision reranking) against Acme's internal dataset and latency SLOs.
- Duration: 4 weeks (internal testing + customer validation) — target start: Mon 2026-03-02, end: Fri 2026-03-27.
- Success criteria (high-level):
  - Latency: 95th percentile inference latency < 300ms for 1–2k concurrent users (on Dedicated instance)
  - Quality: Precision@5 improvement >= 8% vs current baseline on the provided eval set
  - Cost guidance: projected token cost per 1k requests within agreed budget (TBD in week 1)
- Evaluation plan: Marcus will run a baseline run in week 1 and provide comparison dashboard; Acme will validate on 2 sample workflows in week 3.

Ownership / RACI (initial):
- Redwood infra provisioning / onboarding: Marcus Lin (R) — will provision Dedicated trial capacity and provide runbook.
- App integration (client side): Tom Hayes (A) / Rachel Turner (S) — Acme to provide API access + example request traces.
- Security & compliance review: Naomi Feldman (C) — will provide SOC2 summary and handle any evidence requests.
- Procurement / contract: procurement@acmehealth.com (I) — commercial terms and PO.
- POC success sign-off: Rachel Turner (A) / Aditya Rao (C)

Attachments: I attached a quick workbook (poc-success-criteria.xlsx) with the proposed measurable metrics plus a SOC2 executive summary (redwood-soc2-summary.pdf).

Immediate next steps (action owners):
1) Rachel/Tom: Share a sample dataset (anonymized) and expected request volume by Fri 2026-02-20. (Owner: Acme)
2) Marcus: Provision trial Dedicated instance and share onboarding credentials + runbook by Wed 2026-02-24. (Owner: Marcus)
3) Naomi: Send SOC2 + data handling notes and proposed encryption/KMS options by Wed 2026-02-24. (Owner: Naomi)
4) Aditya: Draft a one-page mutual action plan and timeline and circulate by Mon 2026-02-23. (Owner: Aditya)
5) Procurement: Share any PO or contract timeline constraints by Mon 2026-02-23. (Owner: Procurement)

Please confirm or suggest edits. If everyone is aligned I’ll follow up with a short Google Doc (shared link) with the RACI table and the formal timeline.

Cheers,
Aditya

Quick update on tech side and proposed RACI nuance:

Technical plan (high level):
- Week 0 (provisioning, w/c 2026-03-02): Provision Dedicated trial GPU pool, install inference runtime, set up network peering / VPC endpoints (if required), and provide credentials and client SDK.
- Week 1 (baseline): Run Redwood baseline on Acme sample traces; produce latency + quality dashboard.
- Week 2 (integration): Work with Tom to validate request/response contract and iterate on prompts/config.
- Week 3 (stress + validation): Run concurrent load tests and final validation with Acme sample workflows.
- Week 4 (wrap): Compile final results and sign-off doc.

RACI updates (suggested):
- Redwood (Marcus): Responsible for provisioning, baseline runs, and performance tuning (R)
- Acme App (Tom): Responsible for client integration and providing request traces (R)
- Acme Product (Rachel): Accountable for final success sign-off (A)
- Security (Naomi): Consulted for evidence and any additional encryption/KMS requirements (C)
- Aditya: Informed for commercial check-ins and success alignment (I)
- Procurement: Informed / Accountable for PO issuance on Acme side (A/I)

I’ll prepare the onboarding runbook and a minimal checklist (network ports, sample cURLs, test payloads) and upload it to the shared Drive by EOD Tue 2026-02-24. I’ll also include a small script to run the baseline locally if they prefer.

Let me know if we should add an SRE on call for the load tests — happy to loop in the infra team if Acme wants higher concurrency.
